overview.briefing: Review repeated sign-in failures on the accounts server, investigate an unrecognized process, and reconnect the reception workstation.

alerts.title: Repeated failed sign-ins
alerts.evidence: 412 failed sign-in attempts from one address within 10 minutes.
alerts.explanation: Repeated attempts may indicate someone is trying to guess an account password.
steps: Ask the administrator to review account lockout and multi-factor authentication.

alerts.title: Unrecognized executable
alerts.evidence: A previously unseen executable started from the user's temporary folder.
alerts.explanation: Programs launched from temporary folders need review, especially when the user does not recognize them.
steps: Confirm whether the user installed new software.
Review the process path and file signature.
Follow your incident procedure if the file cannot be verified.

alerts.title: Unusual outbound traffic
alerts.evidence: Outbound traffic exceeded the demo baseline for 15 minutes.
alerts.explanation: A large transfer can be normal, but an unexpected destination should be checked.
steps: Identify the destination and originating device.
Confirm whether a backup or software update was running.

alerts.title: Monitoring agent disconnected
alerts.evidence: The endpoint has not reported for 25 minutes.
alerts.explanation: Monitoring has a gap while this endpoint is disconnected.
steps: Check that the computer is powered on and connected.
Ask the administrator to check the monitoring agent.

alerts.title: Sensitive configuration changed
alerts.evidence: File integrity monitoring detected a change to a protected configuration file.
alerts.explanation: Configuration changes should match an approved maintenance task.
steps: Compare the change with the maintenance log.

alerts.title: Suspicious privileged process
alerts.evidence: A new process requested elevated permissions outside the maintenance window.
alerts.explanation: Unexpected elevated processes may put financial records at risk.
steps: Verify the process owner and purpose.
Escalate to your administrator if the activity is not approved.

alerts.title: Network discovery activity
alerts.evidence: One device attempted connections to several internal ports.
alerts.explanation: Discovery traffic may be an approved scan or an unexpected device exploring the network.
steps: Check whether a scan was scheduled.
Identify the device before deciding on a response.

alerts.title: Software update verified
alerts.evidence: An application change matched an approved software update.
alerts.explanation: The administrator verified this change as expected activity.
steps: Keep the update record with the incident notes.

findings.title: Outdated web service
findings.guidance: Review the installed version and schedule an approved update.

findings.title: Missing browser security headers
findings.guidance: Ask the website administrator to review response headers.

findings.title: Management port exposed internally
findings.guidance: Limit management access to approved administrators.

findings.title: Legacy TLS configuration
findings.guidance: The demo administrator updated the TLS configuration.

findings.title: Application version disclosed
findings.guidance: Version details were removed from the demo response headers.

services.name: Groq
services.detail: Local guidance remains available in the demo
